answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A ripple delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A ember check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A tundra penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 4785 identities need 4785 bonds of 12 tokens, 59138 dollars of hardware and 43 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
